recognize_zh: 箭頭所指為細長、兩端尖細、呈新月或鐮刀形的紅血球（drepanocytes），同一視野還有多個船形細胞與一顆有核紅血球，符合鐮刀型紅血球。
features: Elongated crescent-shaped red cells with pointed ends at both poles (arrows)
Additional boat-shaped and oat-shaped poikilocytes throughout the field
Nucleated red blood cell with dense pyknotic nucleus
Scattered target cells; many red cells show crenation (echinocytic change), likely a preparation artifact
Tiny dark punctate dots within many red cells, of uncertain significance at this resolution
Granulocytic precursor/myeloid cell with granular cytoplasm and adequate platelets
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows multiple sickle cells (drepanocytes), characterized by elongated crescent shapes with pointed ends, together with boat-shaped poikilocytes and occasional target cells. A nucleated red blood cell and a granulocytic cell are present. Many red cells show crenation, most likely a drying or storage artifact, and small punctate dots are seen in some red cells whose nature cannot be confirmed at this resolution. Findings are consistent with a sickling disorder such as sickle cell anemia.

ddx.vs: Elliptocytes are oval with blunt rounded ends and even hemoglobin, lacking the sharp pointed tips of sickle cells.
Dacrocytes have a single tapered tail with a rounded body, whereas drepanocytes taper to points at both ends.
HbC and HbSC show intracellular hexagonal or blunt crystals and abundant target cells rather than classic thin crescent sickle cells; hemoglobin HPLC confirms.
Schistocytes are small angular fragments with straight cut edges and are usually accompanied by thrombocytopenia, not elongated intact crescents.
